primary_source.citation: Wang X, Wang Z, Pan J, et al. Patterns of Extrathoracic Metastases in Different Histological Types of Lung Cancer. Front Oncol. 2020;10:715.
primary_source.study_type: Population-based SEER analysis; n=159,241 lung cancer patients diagnosed 2010-2014

biomarkers.name: RB1
biomarkers.clinical_use: Very common; combined TP53 + RB1 inactivation defines canonical SCLC biology

biomarkers.name: MYC amplification (MYC, MYCN, MYCL)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Associates with MYC-driven biology, including SCLC-N enrichment; therapeutic implications such as Aurora kinase inhibitor sensitivity remain investigational

biomarkers.name: DLL3
biomarkers.clinical_use: Tarlatamab (BiTE targeting DLL3) approved for previously treated extensive-stage SCLC

biomarkers.name: PD-L1 (TPS)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Atezolizumab or durvalumab combined with chemotherapy first-line ES-SCLC regardless of PD-L1

biomarkers.name: SLFN11
biomarkers.clinical_use: Associated with response to DNA-damaging agents (including platinum/etoposide and PARP inhibitor strategies); investigational

biomarkers.name: Molecular subtypes: SCLC-A (ASCL1), SCLC-N (NEUROD1), SCLC-P (POU2F3), SCLC-I (inflamed)
biomarkers.prevalence: Approximate and cohort-dependent; SCLC-A is most common, SCLC-N and SCLC-I are intermediate-frequency, SCLC-P is least common
biomarkers.clinical_use: Emerging framework guiding therapy — SCLC-I appears relatively more immunotherapy-responsive; SCLC-P often DLL3-low

biomarkers.name: ProGRP (pro-gastrin-releasing peptide)
biomarkers.clinical_use: More specific than NSE for SCLC

biomarkers.name: NOTCH family alterations
biomarkers.clinical_use: Recurrent loss-of-function pathway alterations support neuroendocrine differentiation biology; not a routine clinical selection biomarker

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: Small cells with scant cytoplasm, high N:C ratio, salt-and-pepper chromatin, nuclear moulding, very high mitotic index, extensive crush artefact
variants: molecular subtypes: SCLC-A (ASCL1), SCLC-N (NEUROD1), SCLC-P (POU2F3), SCLC-I (inflamed)

tumor_microenvironment.immune_context: Traditionally 'cold' — MHC-I loss common; SCLC-I subtype is inflamed and relatively more IO-responsive
tumor_microenvironment.stromal_features: Minimal stroma; extensive necrosis; Azzopardi phenomenon (DNA encrustation of vessel walls)

cellular_states_and_lineage.cell_of_origin: Pulmonary neuroendocrine cells (PNEC) — cells of the diffuse neuroendocrine system in bronchial epithelium
cellular_states_and_lineage.developmental_lineage: Endoderm — foregut derivative with neuroendocrine differentiation
cellular_states_and_lineage.differentiation_state: High-grade neuroendocrine — synaptophysin, chromogranin, INSM1, ASCL1 (SCLC-A) or NEUROD1 (SCLC-N); high proliferation with extensive necrosis
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity: Four transcriptomic subtypes reflect distinct lineage states: SCLC-A (ASCL1+, classic neuroendocrine), SCLC-N (NEUROD1+, mixed), SCLC-P (POU2F3+, tuft cell-like, DLL3-low), SCLC-I (inflamed, relatively more IO-responsive)
